get.description:
Return OHLCV bars for ``symbol`` over the requested date range.

For a cagg-served granularity the response carries ``is_stale``, probed
against the exact view the bars came from (slice 185 D7). ``M1``/``D1`` read
raw hypertables, so no probe is issued and ``is_stale`` is always ``False``.

Windows are admitted before any database work (186 D4): a reversed range or
one whose estimated bar count exceeds the configured ceiling is a ``422``,
not a slow ``500``.

``prints`` defaults to ``eligible`` (slice 173): tape-eligible bars at every
granularity, the rollups holding eligible values and the daily family
serving its EOD bars. ``prints=all`` (raw prints) is served at ``1m`` only;
any other granularity is a ``422``.

parameters.description: eligible (the default): tape-eligible bars at every granularity. all: raw prints, served at 1m only.
parameters.name: prints

schema.description: eligible (the default): tape-eligible bars at every granularity. all: raw prints, served at 1m only.

504.description: The database cancelled the query at the server's statement timeout. Narrow the requested range or use a coarser granularity.

get.description:
Return the day's EODHD credit position.

Always 200 (D6/SC6): an unset key is a setting and an unreachable
provider is a reported condition, so both arrive as ``error`` text with
``credits: null`` rather than as an HTTP failure.

**No** ``GATEWAY_TIMEOUT_RESPONSE`` here, deliberately (D8). This route
issues no statement and takes no parameters, so a statement timeout is
not among its outcomes and the shared constant's remedy — "narrow the
requested range or use a coarser granularity" — would be false advice in
the published schema. Do not add it for symmetry with the sibling route.

No ``Depends(get_db)`` either: the route needs no connection, and the pool
is small enough (``max_size=8``) that holding one across a third party's
response time would be a real cap on concurrency.

The fetch runs on the app's own credit executor rather than the default
pool,
so a provider that will not answer cannot hold threads ``/api/v1/overview``
and ``/api/v1/bars`` need (D8). That is measured behavior, not caution —
see the executor's own docstring for the figure.
One contract's session-bounded bars over ``[start, end)`` sessions.

get.description:
Liveness/readiness probe.

Returns HTTP 200 in every case — callers distinguish database state via
the ``db`` and ``tick_db`` fields of the body, not the status code.

``coverage`` is a coarse pipeline-health signal: exactly the two coverage
caggs behind ``data_status`` (slice 185 D6), not a probe of all seven
bar-serving caggs. Per-granularity truth belongs to the bars endpoint's own
``is_stale`` field.

``tick_db`` (231 TD7) is the tick pool's state; a tick outage never changes
the primary fields. The blocking primary probe runs in the executor and the
tick probe is awaited.

An unknown or non-matching ``symbol`` is a 200 with ``rows: []`` (D5) —
``scope`` still reports ``"symbol"`` so a client can tell "filtered scope,
nothing matched" from "whole registry".

DB failures are not caught here (D9): the freshness probes never raise (a
failed probe is a stale verdict), and a genuine ``data_status`` query
failure propagates to the global 500 handler in ``app.py``.

The ``tick`` block (231 TD7) is read concurrently on the tick pool and
never fails the route: an outage or a refused read is the block's state.
